principle.title: Validated-probe requirement for radical assignment
principle.claim: Radical-trap inhibition in the Seed is non-diagnostic unless trap competence, adduct identity, catalyst compatibility, and product stability are established; the supplied TEMPO, BHT, and 1,1-diphenylethylene outcomes neither establish nor exclude a radical contribution.
mechanistic_basis: The Seed reports TEMPO inhibition but differential BHT and 1,1-diphenylethylene behavior.
No elementary radical step is established.
Transferred assessments explicitly classify BHT and TEMPO outcomes as non-diagnostic without probe-validation controls.
Transferred non-radical TEMPO reactivity illustrates a concrete alternative interpretation.
applicable_electrophile_families: Seed fluorinated carbonyl substrates and their proposed or observed fluorinated intermediates
principle.required_reactive_form: A demonstrably competent radical probe or clock that survives the complete reaction mixture and has known trapping kinetics relative to productive turnover.
catalyst_requirements: Use the complete grounded Pd/base system for diagnostic experiments.
Verify that each probe persists and does not independently poison Pd, consume the donor, or destroy the product.
condition_window: Pd168 identifier, KHCO3, DCE, 80 °C, N2 for Seed-relevant tests.
Use graded probe loadings and matched probe-free controls.
Include catalyst-only, substrate-only, donor-only, product-resubjection, and independently initiated radical controls.
Calibrate analytical response for substrate, desired product, over-defluorinated product, and any adduct.
structural_promoters: A clock positioned at the proposed radical center.
A trap furnishing an unambiguous, atom-mapped adduct.
Orthogonal detection capable of distinguishing trapping from catalyst inhibition.
structural_inhibitors: Probe reaction with the organoboron donor or carbonyl group.
Radical clocks whose rearrangement is slower than recombination or productive capture.
known_exceptions: A cage-confined or metal-bound radical may evade conventional traps.
Probe coordination or oxidation can inhibit catalysis without trapping a substrate radical.
Absence of a reported alkane or adduct is not evidence that no radical formed.
TEMPO can react by non-radical pathways with sufficiently polarized intermediates.
predicted_failure_modes: False-positive radical assignment from catalyst poisoning.
False-negative assignment from slow trapping or incomplete adduct analysis.
Quantitation errors from uncalibrated mass-spectrometric response.
principle.experimental_consequence: Different radical probes may suppress conversion without giving the same adduct or clock response if inhibition arises from Pd binding, donor interception, or product destruction; only a validated radical clock or structurally assigned adduct with matching kinetics would support radical participation.
principle.falsifying_experiment: Run a validated radical clock and graded TEMPO/BHT experiments while quantifying probe recovery, assigned adducts, Pd speciation, donor consumption, product stability, and reaction rate. A clock response or adduct mass balance kinetically coupled to product formation would falsify the claim that existing inhibition is merely non-diagnostic by resolving it in favor of radical participation; normal turnover with a demonstrably competent fast trap would resolve it against a kinetically relevant free-radical pathway.

rejected.reason: Reaction Principle requires a transferable or conditional assessment
rejected.disposition: excluded; caution only, not a transferred principle
